main.arc: It began as an embedded terminal that could hold a Claude session and a git worktree in the same place. It now writes summaries, shares whole sessions through git, runs on Windows, and turns your repo's history into a narrated storyline.

eras.blurb: The terminal learned to run both Claude and OpenCode, hold several sessions at once, recover worktrees, and let an LLM write the design context into the commit message.
eras.title: Two backends, many sessions, and commits that explain themselves

eras.blurb: Sessions got locked into bubblewrap on Linux, learned to travel between contributors with a consent prompt, and the whole thing became aGiTrack.
eras.title: Sandboxes, sharing, and the great renaming

eras.blurb: Native Windows support with a real installer, git moved off the UI thread, and polling learned to back off when nobody's looking.
eras.title: Windows, an MSI, and background threads that stop poking the disk

eras.blurb: aGiTrack learned to cover an agent's own commits with a persistent watermark, and `--backtrace` reconstructed coding history from repos it was never watching.
eras.title: Background mode and reading history backwards

eras.blurb: The dashboard shipped as a static export with a personalized learning page, while a long hunt fixed token counting, atomic writes, and daemons that wouldn't stay up.
eras.title: Learning pages, static dashboards, and honest token counts

eras.blurb: Commits became a browsable narrative with date filtering, external tools got recorded in metadata, and a truncated mouse report stopped hanging the TUI.
eras.title: The storyline, external tool tracking, and a much calmer parser
